statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 venues remain inside the CME weekend halt, with Tail at its structural floor and Stress high.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold. CME equity futures are halted until Sunday 22:00Z, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop at any point in this horizon. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this assessment.
headline: Nasdaq-100 carries a record 30,807.93 close into a second weekend-halt day: a completed Friday retracement and a 15.31 VIX keep Tail at its floor, while a 5.281% 10-year, Brent at $102.25 and an unresolved Hormuz keep Stress high
body: Friday 2 October closed the Nasdaq-100 at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00%, but the close sat 209.60 points below the 31,017.53 session high and only 70.86 above the 30,737.07 low. The session therefore ended with its retracement completed rather than holding an extreme, and that distinction matters more for this contract than the record itself: extreme-holding is a Tail amplifier, a completed give-back is not. VIX fell 6.59% to 15.31 and settled at the bottom of its 15.30-16.24 range, so realised volatility decayed into the close. September payrolls arrived at 29,000 against roughly 90,000 expected, with the unemployment rate up to 4.2% from 4.1%, and bond traders cut the implied probability of an October hike to about 16% from roughly 64% a week earlier. The broader tape confirmed the risk-positive reading: the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.19% to 27,190.86, the S&P 500 added 0.73% to 7,722.72 and the Dow gained 0.49% to 51,176.96, with Nvidia printing an intraday record 237.87 dollars per share at roughly 5.72 trillion dollars of market value. Against that, the long end still rose: the 10-year finished near 5.281% and the 30-year near 5.63%, while the Federal Reserve H.15 release put the 2-year at 4.78% as of 1 October. Energy remains the standing stress input. Brent settled at $102.25 and WTI at $91.11 even after the G7 confirmed a 100 million barrel release of diesel, gasoline and crude from emergency reserves over four months, with a frontloaded diesel tranche promised inside 20 days. The Strait of Hormuz situation is unresolved, with three tankers reported struck by unidentified projectiles on 30 September, transit still disputed and a third U.S. carrier strike group deployed to the region. No verified weekend development has altered any of these inputs. Every hour of this horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt that began Friday at 21:00Z and runs until the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop within the window and Tail stays at its structural floor while Stress stays high on carry that cannot be hedged until a venue reopens. The shared Finviz context file was read and found stale at four days old with a partial collection status, so it contributed no evidence to this assessment and full independent research was used instead.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span Friday's U.S. cash session and the first hours of the weekend halt. Published Claude history shows Tail peaking in an orange 25-27 band across the 13:00-14:00Z cash-open hours, easing to a yellow 20-24 through the afternoon, then falling into green single digits from 21:00Z as the cash close completed its retracement and CME futures entered the halt. Stress held in a high 71-79 band through the session on the energy and long-end backdrop before easing toward 65, and Confidence ranged between 82 and 89. These are the model's own published opinions at the time and are not restated with hindsight.
outlookSummary: Every hour of this horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, which began Friday at 21:00Z and runs until the Sunday 22:00Z reopen, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop and the mapped state is green throughout. Tail holds flat at 8 through the Saturday slots and steps to 9 from 19:00Z purely on unpriced weekend headline risk accumulating behind a closed market, not on any observed structure. Stress eases from 65 to 63 through the dead Saturday hours, then firms to 68 by the end of the window as a 5.281% 10-year, Brent at $102.25, an unresolved Hormuz situation and the pending G7 implementation detail are all carried forward unpriced. Confidence decays from 85 to 75 purely as Friday's verified evidence ages with no live NQ reference to refresh it. The dominant mode shifts from normal to mixed for the Sunday slots to reflect genuinely two-sided unpriced risk rather than observed conflict. Both genuine checkpoints lie beyond this window: Monday's ISM Services PMI at 14:00Z on 5 October and Wednesday's FOMC Minutes at 18:00Z on 7 October.
